quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #18
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: The road curves right ahead. Slow down to 35 mph.
A divided highway is starting. Slow down to 35 mph.
Merge ahead. Slow down to 35 mph.
The road winds ahead. Slow down to 35 mph.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road curves right ahead. Slow down to 35 mph.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you the road curves right. You must slow down to the safe speed shown, which is 35 mph.

questions.question: When driving past a parked car on the side of the road, you should:

options.text: Expect the driver to open the car door as you pass.
Speed up.
Slam on your brakes.
Assume the driver will wait for you to pass before opening the door.

questions.correctAnswerText: Expect the driver to open the car door as you pass.
questions.explanation: Assume the driver will open their door as you approach. Always drive carefully near parked cars.

questions.question: When can you turn right on a red traffic light?

options.text: When there is a sign that says no right turn on red.
Before pedestrians have crossed the intersection.
Before coming to a complete stop.
After you stop completely and yield to pedestrians and other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: After you stop completely and yield to pedestrians and other vehicles.
questions.explanation: You may turn right on red only after a full stop. Make sure no sign forbids it. Always yield to pedestrians and traffic in the intersection.

questions.question: Which statement is true about passing?

options.text: Signal at least 100 feet before changing lanes. Check for oncoming traffic.
Use your mirrors and look over your left shoulder to check your blind spot.
See both headlights of the other car in your rearview mirror before moving back to your lane.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: When passing, signal at least 100 feet ahead. Check your mirrors and look over your shoulder. Wait to see both headlights of the other car in your mirror before returning to your lane.

questions.question: Roads freeze quickest when they are:

options.text: Flat.
Curvy.
In direct sunlight.
In the shade.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the shade.
questions.explanation: Shaded areas freeze faster than sunny areas. Shade from trees and buildings keeps roads colder. These spots also take longer to dry.

questions.question: To make a right turn, your car should be:

options.text: Near the center of the street.
Close to the left side of the street.
Close to the right side of the street.
Past the center of the intersection when you start turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Close to the right side of the street.
questions.explanation: Move to the right side of the road before turning right. Do not cut across lanes.

questions.question: When should you signal before passing another vehicle?

options.text: Just before changing lanes.
At any time.
After changing lanes.
Early enough so other drivers know what you plan to do.

questions.correctAnswerText: Early enough so other drivers know what you plan to do.
questions.explanation: Signal early so other drivers have time to know your passing intentions.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: All traffic must turn right.
No right turn allowed.
All traffic must go straight.
A road is joining from the right.

questions.correctAnswerText: A road is joining from the right.
questions.explanation: This sign warns of an intersection ahead where a road joins from the right.

questions.question: When a driver behind you wants to pass, you should:

options.text: Speed up.
Keep the same speed.
Slow down to give them room to pass safely.
Change lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down to give them room to pass safely.
questions.explanation: Slowing down gives the other driver space to pass. This helps them complete the pass faster and more safely.

questions.question: Which tip does NOT help with safe night driving?

options.text: Keep your windshield clean.
Know that tinted windows reduce visibility at night.
Carry a flashlight in your vehicle.
Look directly into the headlights of oncoming vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look directly into the headlights of oncoming vehicles.
questions.explanation: Looking into oncoming headlights makes your eyes adjust. After the car passes, your eyes need time to readjust. During this time, you cannot see well.

questions.question: When can a driver legally pass on the right side of another vehicle?

options.text: When the vehicle is waiting to turn left and there is an available passing lane.
Even if you have to drive off the pavement.
On a narrow bridge.
At any time.

questions.correctAnswerText: When the vehicle is waiting to turn left and there is an available passing lane.
questions.explanation: You may pass on the right of a vehicle turning left if there is an available passing lane. You may also pass on the right on multilane roads with two or more lanes going the same direction. Never drive off the pavement to pass another vehicle.

questions.question: What do two solid yellow lines on the pavement mean?

options.text: Passing is allowed from both directions.
Passing is not allowed.
Passing is allowed at the top of a hill.
Passing is allowed during daylight only.

questions.correctAnswerText: Passing is not allowed.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines mean traffic on the other side is moving in the opposite direction. Never cross two solid yellow lines to pass from either direction.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Steep grade ahead.
Pedestrian crossing ahead.
Low ground railroad crossing.
Low clearance.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low clearance.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that the overpass ahead has low clearance. Do not proceed if your vehicle is taller than the height shown on the sign.

questions.question: How can you reduce the risk of hydroplaning?

options.text: Do not speed on wet roads.
Use tires with the correct air pressure.
Replace tires with worn tread.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning occurs when your vehicle slides on a layer of water between the tires and the road. Low tire pressure, worn tread, and speeding all increase the risk of hydroplaning.

questions.question: What should you do when in a travel lane on the roadway?

options.text: You may stop to drop off passengers.
You may stop to look up an address.
You may make a U-turn or back up if you take the wrong freeway entrance ramp.
Keep moving. Do not stop for any reason. Pull off the road safely when you can.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep moving. Do not stop for any reason. Pull off the road safely when you can.
questions.explanation: Never stop in a travel lane. Keep moving until you can safely pull off the road. If you miss your exit, do not back up. Go to the next exit where you can safely turn around.

questions.question: If an oncoming vehicle uses high beams, where should you look?

options.text: Either side of the road
The center of the road
The right side of the road
The left side of the road

questions.correctAnswerText: The right side of the road
questions.explanation: Look toward the right side of the road if an oncoming vehicle uses high beams. This prevents you from being blinded and helps you stay on course until the vehicle passes.

questions.question: What is your blind spot?

options.text: An area you cannot see without moving your head.
The area directly behind your vehicle.
The area you see in your rearview mirror.
The area you see in your side mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: An area you cannot see without moving your head.
questions.explanation: Blind spots are areas you cannot see without turning your head. They are located to the sides and behind your vehicle.

questions.question: What lights should you use when driving in fog?

options.text: Parking lights.
Low beams.
High beams.
It does not matter which lights you use.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low beams.
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights when driving in fog, rain, or snow.

questions.question: What do work zone signs mean?

options.text: It is summer.
You must stop immediately and back up.
Driving conditions are not ideal.
You should drive faster to exit the work zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: Driving conditions are not ideal.
questions.explanation: Work zone signs are orange and show that construction or maintenance work is happening on or near the road. Drive carefully when you see these signs.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: School ahead.
School crossing.
Pedestrian crossing.
Construction workers on or near the roadway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pedestrian crossing.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually diamond-shaped with black markings on a yellow background. This sign alerts drivers that pedestrians may be crossing the road ahead.

questions.question: You see a flashing red light at an intersection. What should you do?

options.text: Stop completely, then go when it is safe.
Stop only if other cars are coming to the intersection.
Stop only if other cars are already in the intersection.
Slow down and be ready to stop if needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely, then go when it is safe.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light works like a stop sign. You must stop, let other cars go first, and then go when it is safe.

questions.question: Which statement about speed is true?

options.text: Driving too slowly on certain highways can be dangerous.
Speeding can cause deaths.
Speeding is safe if you are a good driver.
Both driving too slowly on certain highways and speeding can be dangerous.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both driving too slowly on certain highways and speeding can be dangerous.
questions.explanation: Higher speeds make crashes more deadly. At speeds above 80 miles per hour, survival is very unlikely. Driving slower than other traffic is also dangerous because other drivers may take unsafe risks to pass you.

questions.question: To check your blind spot before changing lanes to the left, look:

options.text: Over your right shoulder.
At your side mirror.
Over your left shoulder.
At your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Over your left shoulder.
questions.explanation: To check your blind spot, look over your shoulder in the direction you want to go.

questions.question: When driving in rain, you must use:

options.text: Low beam headlights.
High beam headlights.
Parking lights.
No lights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use your low beam headlights when driving in rain.

questions.question: Night driving requires extra caution because:

options.text: Traffic moves faster at night.
There is more traffic at night.
Drivers cannot see as well at night.
Accidents happen more often at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers cannot see as well at night.
questions.explanation: It is dark at night, so drivers cannot see as well as they do during the day. You must use your headlights from 30 minutes after sunset until 30 minutes before sunrise, or whenever vehicles cannot be seen from 500 feet away.
